overall.pentacles.09.reversed.do: If you're going to use a new place or take part in something, check for yourself that what you'll need is actually available.
overall.pentacles.09.reversed.pause: Don't assure others that a place is good just because it looks appealing. Find out whether it's inconvenient to use before recommending it.

overall.pentacles.09.upright.headline: You could enjoy the comfort you've worked to secure.
flow: What you've done could help you have a satisfying day. You may finish what you need easily on your own and have enough available that you don't need to wait for help. It's a good day to make time for something enjoyable you've put off.
If you've finished something well, mark it in a way you enjoy. There's no need to attend something you don't want to just to impress other people.
overall.pentacles.09.upright.do: Celebrate finishing something well by doing what you've wanted to do but haven't had time for.
overall.pentacles.09.upright.pause: Don't force yourself to attend something you don't want to just to show other people you're doing well.

overall.pentacles.10.reversed.headline: One overambitious choice could disrupt things that were going well.
flow: A decision based on luck alone could bring unexpected setbacks today. Abruptly changing something familiar that works or making several commitments depend on one result may cause a series of problems. Choose carefully so you don't lose everything you've built up at once.
Try something new on a small scale while keeping what you're already doing. You don't need to change everything just because someone says it will go well.
overall.pentacles.10.reversed.do: If you want to change the method for something that's going well, test the new one on a small part before changing the whole thing.
overall.pentacles.10.reversed.pause: Don't make several commitments you can only keep if a result you're waiting for goes well. If it turns out differently, those promises could become difficult to keep too.

overall.pentacles.10.upright.headline: Long-standing connections and experience could give you solid support.
flow: Things may go steadily when you're with familiar people today. Old records or experience could supply information you don't know, and people around you may help with a difficulty. What you've built up could prove useful without a fresh effort from scratch.
Look for information you organised before or draw on the experience of someone you've known a long time. With reliable help available, you don't need to start everything over.
overall.pentacles.10.upright.do: If you have a new problem to solve, look back through information you've organised before for something useful. Records you've kept over time may already contain the answer you need.
overall.pentacles.10.upright.pause: If someone you've known a long time can help, don't struggle to work out everything unfamiliar from scratch on your own.

overall.pentacles.11.reversed.headline: A distraction could make you miss an opportunity you need.
flow: Tasks may slip behind and expected news could disappoint you today. Spending time on something fun may make you read an important notice late, or a new activity could quickly seem uninteresting. You may make a mistake that a little more checking would have prevented.
Read the notices that need attention now first. If there's something you've wanted to try, complete the necessary first steps before deciding it's boring.
overall.pentacles.11.reversed.do: Before spending time on other things, check the information you've put off reading for anything you need to answer or deal with now.
overall.pentacles.11.reversed.pause: Don't dismiss a new activity as pointless and give it up before completing the necessary steps just because it soon feels uninteresting.

overall.pentacles.11.upright.headline: Something you learn could prove useful in practice.
flow: Looking into something carefully could give you a useful answer today. You may learn a method and use it straight away or hear news containing information you need. Even if the first step is small, the day favours steady progress.
Try a newly learned method on something simple. Don't dismiss an explanation as something you already know before you've heard it all.
overall.pentacles.11.upright.do: If you've learned a new method, start by trying one of the simpler tasks it can be used for.
overall.pentacles.11.upright.pause: Don't stop listening to an explanation because it sounds familiar. The rest may include something you don't yet know.

overall.pentacles.12.reversed.headline: Postponed tasks could make even small things troublesome.
flow: Something you've been doing may make little progress today. Neglecting a familiar task could lead to omissions, or restarting something you've put off may take time. Your usual method may no longer fit the current situation either.
Check how things stand with one task you haven't touched for a while. Repeatedly putting things aside to do all at once later could leave even more unfinished.
overall.pentacles.12.reversed.do: If you've put a task off for a long time, check how far you got. You may find something missing even in parts you thought were done.
overall.pentacles.12.reversed.pause: Don't put off an unfinished task again by telling yourself you'll do it all at once later. Leaving it longer can mean spending time working out where you left off.

overall.pentacles.12.upright.headline: You could finish what you set out to do, even at a slow pace.
flow: It's a good day to handle familiar tasks reliably. You may not see a dramatic change, but you could deliver what you promised and earn trust through steady work. You should be able to finish what's needed today without rushing.
Finish things one by one in the order you've been following. Abruptly changing methods because someone else finished faster could create extra trouble.
overall.pentacles.12.upright.do: Finish familiar tasks one by one in your usual order, checking that you've completed everything you promised.
overall.pentacles.12.upright.pause: Don't abruptly change a method that's been working because someone else finished faster. If your usual order lets you finish, you don't need to match their pace.

overall.pentacles.13.reversed.headline: Unnecessary suspicion could create more work for you.
flow: Even something that's fine may feel hard to trust today, making things more troublesome. Repeated questions about a confirmed fact or doubts about someone's offer of help could stall a conversation. Changing your choice without a clear reason may leave things less convenient than before.
Check specifically what's worrying you. Once you've had an answer, decide on the basis of what you've confirmed instead of repeating the same suspicion.
overall.pentacles.13.reversed.do: If you're uneasy about a decision ahead, ask specifically about the conditions worrying you and decide based on the answer.
overall.pentacles.13.reversed.pause: Don't keep questioning why someone wants to help when you have no reason to distrust them. If you only question their intentions, it can be hard to talk about the help they could actually give.

overall.pentacles.13.upright.headline: Having what you need could make the day comfortable.
flow: Other people's consideration could help the day pass smoothly. You may find a necessary item or place without difficulty and finish delayed household chores more easily than expected. You could even have enough time or resources to look after someone else.
If you have more than enough of something, share it with someone who needs it. Help you can give easily is enough, without doing so much that you can't finish your own tasks.
overall.pentacles.13.upright.do: If you have plenty of an item, it's fine to share it with someone who needs it. Start with what you can easily give while keeping enough for your own use.
overall.pentacles.13.upright.pause: Don't postpone your own tasks to look after someone else. Consider what you need to finish and offer only as much help as you can comfortably give.

overall.pentacles.14.reversed.headline: Wanting more could cost you something you've already gained.
flow: Chasing better terms could make things go wrong today. You may add demands after receiving a satisfactory answer or accept something beyond your means to keep up appearances. Choosing what looks successful over what actually benefits you could leave a burden behind.
Once the terms are good enough, decide where to stop. Don't tell people you can do something beyond your ability just to impress them.
overall.pentacles.14.reversed.do: If you've received terms you're satisfied with, settle on those instead of adding demands to get more.
overall.pentacles.14.reversed.pause: Don't accept more than you can handle just to show others how capable you are. First consider whether you have the time and energy to finish the task.

overall.pentacles.14.upright.headline: A choice based on experience could bring a satisfying result.
flow: Something you know how to do in practice could bring good results today. Experience may help you solve a seemingly complicated problem and get what you need to finish without strain. An experienced person could offer specific help too.
Start with a method you've used before instead of making bold promises. A proven approach may suit the situation better than an eye-catching new one.
overall.pentacles.14.upright.do: If you need to solve a complicated problem, choose a method that worked before and still fits, then try it.
overall.pentacles.14.upright.pause: Even if a new method looks impressive, don't promise it will work as though you've confirmed its results when you've never tried it.

overall.swords.01.reversed.headline: A message passed on incorrectly could send things the wrong way.
flow: A small misunderstanding could complicate things today. Something you thought you'd said clearly may be passed on with a different meaning, or you may need to recheck instructions you've misunderstood. A conclusion reached too quickly may be overturned.
For an important message, ask whether the other person understood what you meant. If you discover an error, correcting it before explaining yourself could save trouble.
overall.swords.01.reversed.do: After saying something important, ask what the other person understood you to mean. They may have taken it differently even if you thought you were clear.
overall.swords.01.reversed.pause: If you discover you've passed on something incorrect, don't begin with a long defence of yourself. Correcting the error first can keep the other person from making a mistaken decision.

overall.swords.01.upright.headline: Something confusing could become clear and a difficult problem could be solved.
flow: It's a good day to discover why something has been troubling you. Sorting through conflicting accounts could reveal the facts and make a difficult decision easier. You may get a clear answer to a problem that's dragged on.
Once you know the conclusion, tell the people who need it clearly. Start with the facts you've confirmed, instead of adding so much explanation that the main point gets lost.
overall.swords.01.upright.do: If you don't know what caused a problem, compare the facts you've confirmed from the different accounts.
overall.swords.01.upright.pause: Don't dwell on background details when sharing what you've found out. Start with the facts the other person needs so your conclusion comes across clearly.

overall.swords.02.reversed.headline: Conflicting accounts could lead you to make the wrong judgement.
flow: Listening to several people could make things more complicated today. You may be asked to make a decision you've put off, only for new information to contradict what you've heard. Choosing anything just to get it over with could leave problems to deal with afterwards.
Ask specifically about the part that needs a decision now. Checking with the person involved will be less confusing than asking more people about the same story.
overall.swords.02.reversed.do: If several people's accounts differ, ask the person directly involved specifically about the issue you need to decide now.
overall.swords.02.reversed.pause: Don't pick any option just to get a complicated discussion over with. Accepting terms you don't understand could leave you with more to sort out later.

overall.swords.02.upright.headline: An uncertain choice could delay a decision.
flow: Something important may be hard to settle today. Either of two options could leave you disappointed, or not knowing the other person's answer may make it difficult to act first. If a necessary fact is missing, thinking longer may not produce an answer.
Start by checking one piece of information you need for the decision. Instead of letting someone rush you into choosing, it's fine to ask how long you can wait.
overall.swords.02.upright.do: If you don't know which option to choose, ask someone familiar with the situation about the information you still need to decide.
overall.swords.02.upright.pause: Don't give a definite answer before you understand the circumstances just because you're being rushed. Ask how long they can wait and request time to think.

overall.swords.03.reversed.headline: Resolving something hurtful could make the day a little easier.
flow: Something that's been weighing on your mind could trouble you less today. You may correct a story that was passed on wrongly or receive an apology for something that hurt you. Things can become less uncomfortable even if you don't return to how you were straight away.
If the other person wants to explain, hear as much as you feel able to. Decide how to proceed instead of arguing again about something you've already resolved.
overall.swords.03.reversed.do: If something hurtful has been resolved, discuss how you'd like to get along from here. It's fine to say if you can't be as close as before straight away.
overall.swords.03.reversed.pause: Don't reopen an argument you've both explained and settled simply because you still feel uneasy about it.

overall.swords.03.upright.headline: An answer you didn't want could leave you disappointed.
flow: Something you've hoped for may not go your way today. A statement you trusted could turn out to be untrue, or you may be turned down for something you thought was certain. Even if you don't want to hear the answer, you need to know it before making your next decision.
Hear the reasons in full before challenging the answer. Taking your hurt out on people who weren't involved could only make more things uncomfortable.
overall.swords.03.upright.do: Even if you didn't get the answer you wanted, hear the reasons in full. Knowing the relevant facts can help you decide what to do next.
overall.swords.03.upright.pause: Don't speak sharply to people who had nothing to do with disappointing news. Taking your hurt out on them could make those relationships uncomfortable too.

overall.swords.04.reversed.headline: Something that was on hold could start again and keep you busy.
flow: You may hear news again about something that's been quiet. A delayed request could receive an answer, or you may get a chance to return to something you set aside for a while. Trying to do as much as before all at once could be harder than you expect.
When you start again, take on the most urgent thing first. A long absence doesn't mean you have to answer every request immediately.
overall.swords.04.reversed.do: If you're returning to something you've set aside for a while, choose the most urgent request first instead of taking on everything that's piled up.
overall.swords.04.reversed.pause: Don't push yourself to do as much as before immediately when you restart. It's fine to build up gradually while you get used to it again.

overall.swords.04.upright.headline: The day is likely to pass quietly without much trouble.
flow: Your luck favours an uneventful day more than a new achievement. Something that's caused a stir may settle down, or there could be fewer demands for an urgent answer. A result you're waiting for may take a little longer, but there may not be much you need to do about it right now.
It's fine to leave something alone for a while if there's no rush. Bringing up a settled matter just because things are quiet could start an unnecessary exchange.
overall.swords.04.upright.do: If there's no urgent reply or further action needed, set aside anything that can wait and take a quiet break.
overall.swords.04.upright.pause: Don't reopen a finished argument to go over who was right or wrong. Exchanging words that don't need saying could make things uncomfortable between you again.

overall.swords.05.reversed.headline: You could put an end to a long-running argument.
flow: There may be a chance to compromise with someone you've been uncomfortable around. If each of you gives a little, you could end the dispute without further loss. You don't have to agree on everything to stop the constant arguing.
Say where you're willing to give way first. Revisiting old remarks after an apology or agreement could restart an argument you've worked hard to end.
overall.swords.05.reversed.do: If a chance to compromise comes up with someone you're on uneasy terms with, say first where you're willing to give way. You may find a way to end the argument without agreeing on everything.
overall.swords.05.reversed.pause: Don't go back over who was wrong after an apology or agreement. Deciding who was more at fault after you've agreed to step back could keep the argument going.

overall.swords.05.upright.headline: Winning an argument could still leave you feeling uncomfortable.
flow: You may argue over something small or hear an unfair remark today. Even if your view is accepted, the other person could remain resentful, leaving you with more lost than won. Insisting on deciding who's right to the bitter end could distance someone you might need help from.
Once you've made your point, stop pressing the other person. You don't need a final remark just to get the better of them.
overall.swords.05.upright.do: Once you've said what needed saying in an argument, try stopping there. Continuing to argue over who's right could harm a relationship where you help each other.
overall.swords.05.upright.pause: Don't belittle someone to make them accept your view. Even if you win the argument, the resentment left behind could make it hard to do things together later.

overall.swords.06.reversed.headline: A problem you thought was solved could come back.
flow: Something you've been trying to leave behind may last longer than expected today. Even with a different approach, an overlooked problem could return, or you may have to take on an old request again. Merely changing where you are could bring the same trouble with you.
Look at the original cause of a problem that returns. Passing it to someone else just to get away for now could mean having to explain it all again later.
overall.swords.06.reversed.do: If a problem you thought was solved keeps returning, check whether any of its original causes still need to be addressed.
overall.swords.06.reversed.pause: Don't pass an unresolved problem to someone else just to escape it for now. If the cause remains, you may have to explain the same problem all over again later.

overall.swords.06.upright.headline: Getting out of a difficult situation could give you some relief.
flow: You may be able to leave an uncomfortable situation today. Someone could help with a problem you couldn't solve alone, or moving somewhere else may reduce the trouble you're dealing with. Not every problem has to be over for things to feel easier than before.
If someone can explain an easier way to move elsewhere, hear them out. It's fine to choose somewhere different if the familiar place has been uncomfortable.
overall.swords.06.upright.do: If someone explains an easier way to handle something you've struggled with alone, hear them out and accept their help.
overall.swords.06.upright.pause: If there's somewhere you could be more at ease, don't keep staying in an uncomfortable place just because it's familiar.

overall.swords.07.reversed.headline: You could put something right and get the help you need.
flow: Previously hidden circumstances could come to light and help solve a problem today. Speaking honestly about something you've struggled on with alone may make it easier to put right than you expect. Another person's advice could also clear up something you've misunderstood.
If you've made a mistake, tell the people who need to know first. Making excuses for something that's already come out could keep even a small problem going.
overall.swords.07.reversed.do: If a mistake is difficult to put right alone, tell the people involved what went wrong before trying to handle it all yourself.
overall.swords.07.reversed.pause: Don't use a convincing excuse to cover up a mistake that's already come to light. Changing your explanation repeatedly could make even a small error take longer to sort out.

overall.swords.07.upright.headline: A different approach could solve something that's been stuck.
flow: You may see another way to handle something that's been difficult to tackle directly. You could get the help you need without a confrontation, or information you've quietly gathered may save you trouble. You don't have to reveal every plan in advance.
For something you haven't decided yet, ask only the people you need to. Don't hide an important condition that could lead someone else to make the wrong decision.
overall.swords.07.upright.do: For something that's hard to resolve, look for another approach by quietly asking only people who know the circumstances.
overall.swords.07.upright.pause: Don't leave out important conditions when you need someone's agreement. You don't have to reveal every plan, but do tell them the facts they need to decide.

overall.swords.08.reversed.headline: Something you thought was impossible could become worth trying.
flow: You may get a chance to move beyond something that's held you back. A condition you thought was essential might not be required, or you could discover another option. Something you've put off for a long time may be easier to start than before.
If you've found a new way to do it, try a small part yourself. A refusal in the past doesn't mean you have to give up this chance too.
overall.swords.08.reversed.do: If another way to tackle something that's been stuck becomes available, use it to try the part you can do now.
overall.swords.08.reversed.pause: If changed conditions let you try again, don't give up this attempt just because you were told no in the past.

overall.swords.08.upright.headline: Restrictions could make it hard to do what you want.
flow: Even small things may not go your way today, leaving you frustrated. You could be left waiting because you haven't received permission or have fewer options available. Assuming that methods you haven't checked won't work either could make things seem even more hopeless.
Check the conditions yourself to see whether something really is impossible. One blocked route doesn't mean you have to give up every other approach.
overall.swords.08.upright.do: If you're told you can't do something you want, ask directly which condition prevents it. Understanding the actual restriction can help you look for another approach.
overall.swords.08.upright.pause: Don't assume every untried method is impossible just because one approach hasn't worked.

overall.swords.09.reversed.headline: A reassuring answer could ease something you've worried about alone.
flow: A problem you've feared may turn out to be less difficult than you expected today. Explaining it could bring help, or you may hear a specific answer to a vague worry. Even if everything isn't solved, what to do right now could become clear.
Tell someone you trust what actually happened. If you only say you're fine, they may find it hard to give you the help you need.
overall.swords.09.reversed.do: If you've been worrying about something alone, tell someone you trust exactly what happened and what worries you about it.
overall.swords.09.reversed.pause: Don't ignore what still needs to be done just because someone's help has reassured you. If you've learned what needs doing now, start with that.

overall.swords.09.upright.headline: Worry could slow down even familiar tasks.
flow: Waiting for something may make it hard to feel at ease today. You could expect the worst from an unanswered question or see a small mistake as a major problem. If that worry carries over into other things, you may overlook something.
Separate what you're afraid of from what you've actually been told. There's no need to announce a failure or cancel plans before you have the result.
overall.swords.09.upright.do: If a late answer has you fearing a bad result, ask yourself whether you've actually been told that result or are only assuming it.
overall.swords.09.upright.pause: Don't announce a failure or cancel plans before the result arrives. You don't yet know whether things have ended the way you fear.

overall.swords.10.reversed.headline: A difficult spell could pass and let you start again.
flow: Something that's gone badly for a while may improve a little today. You could find a remaining chance in something you thought was over, or a responsibility that's been too much may become lighter. Things may not return to normal straight away, but there could be something you can try again.
When you start something new, take on only as much as you can finish comfortably. Accepting the same conditions that were difficult before could bring back the same burden.
overall.swords.10.reversed.do: If you get another chance at something that was difficult, take on less than before so you can finish it without overdoing it now.
overall.swords.10.reversed.pause: Don't accept the same conditions that overwhelmed you before just because another chance has arrived. Check what made it difficult and whether those demands would return.

overall.swords.10.upright.headline: Something that's dragged on could come to a disappointing end.
flow: There may be something you can't continue today. An answer you've hoped for until the end may not arrive, or you could have to stop something you've worked hard on. Trying to force it back to the way it was could make even your remaining tasks hard to manage.
Take care of only what needs clearing up after it's over. Instead of taking on something new to make up for it immediately, keep only what you must finish today.
overall.swords.10.upright.do: If something has become too difficult to continue, finish only the necessary final tasks and leave it there.
overall.swords.10.upright.pause: Don't take on something new to make up for a disappointing result immediately. First check whether you can manage what you still have to do.

overall.swords.11.reversed.headline: Something you haven't checked could catch you off guard.
flow: Unexpected information may disrupt things today. You could believe something too quickly when you first hear it or struggle with a question you aren't prepared for. Passing on an uncertain story could leave you having to explain it yourself.
If you don't know, say you'll check before answering. Even if you're suspicious, don't confront the other person before finding out the facts.
overall.swords.11.reversed.do: If you're asked about something you don't know, ask for time to check and find an accurate answer instead of replying with a guess.
overall.swords.11.reversed.pause: Don't confront someone immediately because a story you've just heard sounds suspicious. There may be circumstances you haven't checked, so find out the facts before discussing it.

overall.swords.11.upright.headline: An overlooked fact could help you avoid a mistake.
flow: Something you nearly passed over could reveal an important fact today. Reading unfamiliar instructions carefully may save unnecessary effort and help you spot incorrect information early. A question asked out of curiosity could help solve something that's been stuck.
Read even the small print when the information is new to you. When passing on what you've learned, stick to what you've checked yourself.
overall.swords.11.upright.do: When reading unfamiliar instructions, check even the small print and ask directly about anything you don't understand.
overall.swords.11.upright.pause: When sharing something you've discovered, don't mix guesses with facts you've checked and present it all as certain.

overall.swords.12.reversed.headline: Something started in haste could stop halfway through.
flow: Mistakes may arise in something you're trying to finish quickly today. You could set off unprepared and have to turn back, or start more than you can manage and fail to finish. Answering quickly because someone is rushing you may create more trouble.
Check you have what you need before setting off. For something you can't finish now, say when you can do it instead of promising you can.
overall.swords.12.reversed.do: If you're going somewhere to do something, check before leaving that you've packed what you'll need. It can save you a return trip for something you've forgotten.
overall.swords.12.reversed.pause: Even if someone wants a quick answer, don't promise to do something immediately when you can't finish it now. Say when you'll actually be able to do it.

overall.swords.12.upright.headline: Something delayed could reach a quick conclusion.
flow: A matter that's dragged on could be resolved sooner than expected today. Stating your wishes clearly may get you the answer you want, and acting promptly could bring progress. Keeping up with the speed of events may make it easy to skip a necessary explanation.
Go ahead with what you've decided, but check that the people involved understand too. If you set off without explaining, they may be slow to follow because they don't know what to do.
overall.swords.12.upright.do: If you've decided what to do about a long-delayed matter, tell the people involved your decision and start with the part you can do first.
overall.swords.12.upright.pause: Don't push ahead alone and skip necessary explanations because things are moving quickly. Give the people involved time to understand what they need to do.

overall.swords.13.reversed.headline: A hasty judgement could lead to an unfair misunderstanding.
flow: One bad impression could lead you to judge wrongly today. You may reach a conclusion before hearing the other person's circumstances, or someone who knows nothing about your situation could misunderstand you. A sharp reply may leave you with even less chance to explain the facts.
When you first hear a story, check whether anything is missing. Disliking someone doesn't mean what they're saying this time must be wrong.
overall.swords.13.reversed.do: If you've heard only one side, consider what circumstances you haven't heard about yet. Listen to the other person's account before judging what happened.
overall.swords.13.reversed.pause: Don't dismiss everything someone says without checking whether it's true just because you usually feel uncomfortable around them.

overall.swords.13.upright.headline: You could sort out something that's become complicated.
flow: It's a good day to find the answer you need without being swayed by confusing accounts. You may recognise unsuitable conditions even when dealing with someone you've known a long time, or bring something unnecessary to a clean end. Some disappointment may remain, but you could make fewer decisions you'll regret later.
If you need to refuse, give a brief reason. Stating the facts doesn't require judging the other person or adding criticism.
overall.swords.13.upright.do: Even if a request comes from someone you've known a long time, briefly explain why you can't accept it if the conditions don't suit you.
overall.swords.13.upright.pause: When refusing because the conditions don't suit you, discuss those conditions without bringing up the person's character or faults.

overall.swords.14.reversed.headline: One-sided demands could put you in a difficult position.
flow: You may meet someone unwilling to listen even when you explain your circumstances today. You could be pushed to accept unsuitable terms or feel unfairly treated by a decision based on only one account. Agreeing immediately because the other person intimidates you may be hard to undo.
For something important, ask for time to check before answering. When you're the one making a decision, let others finish their explanations too.
overall.swords.14.reversed.do: If you can't answer immediately, ask for time to check the details and decide, even if the other person is pressing hard.
overall.swords.14.reversed.pause: Don't interrupt someone's explanation when you're making a decision. Reaching a conclusion before hearing the full circumstances could leave someone feeling unfairly treated.

overall.swords.14.upright.headline: Clear rules could settle something that was uncertain.
flow: Even a much-debated issue may reach a conclusion based on clear standards today. Evidence could settle an argument over who's right, and you may receive a judgement you can trust. If you've prepared your facts properly, you'll be well placed to explain your position.
For an important decision, present information that can be checked instead of relying on a feeling. Trying to change the rules to suit yourself could make a sound judgement harder to reach.
overall.swords.14.upright.do: When giving your view before an important decision, explain your reasons using facts that other people can check too.
overall.swords.14.upright.pause: Don't keep changing the standard to get a result that favours you. Applying the same agreed principles to the same circumstances helps you reach a decision people can accept.

overall.wands.01.reversed.headline: Something you want to start may not get going straight away.
flow: A new venture could start later than expected today. You may be missing some preparation, or have a good idea without a chance to try it yet. Rushing into it could mean stopping soon afterwards to prepare again.
Check what's preventing the start, one thing at a time. Unhelpful timing doesn't mean you have to discard the whole idea.
overall.wands.01.reversed.do: If you're not fully prepared for something you meant to start, check what's missing and do the preparation you can manage now.
overall.wands.01.reversed.pause: Don't give up the whole idea just because there's no opening right now. The timing being wrong today doesn't mean you'll never be able to do it.

overall.wands.01.upright.headline: A new start could receive a good response.
flow: Something you begin today could go better than expected. Trying out an idea may reveal a useful method, and an activity you're interested in could offer a chance to return. Luck also favours starting something you've postponed for a long time.
Begin with the first step you can take now. Learn what you'll need next by trying it, rather than taking on a great deal at once.
overall.wands.01.upright.do: If you've put off something you wanted to try, start with the part you can do now. It's fine to learn what you'll need next by doing it.
overall.wands.01.upright.pause: Don't take on too much at the start of something new. Keeping it manageable gives you a better chance of continuing without having to stop partway.

overall.wands.02.reversed.headline: Hesitation could delay a change you wanted to make.
flow: A good option may be available, but you could find it hard to act on it today. Worries about somewhere unfamiliar may keep you from replying, or you could spend so long comparing that you miss your chance. The day may pass with neither the old plan nor the new one settled.
Check whether the worry holding you back comes from a practical restriction. Ask about what you need to know first, rather than waiting until everything is certain.
overall.wands.02.reversed.do: If you're hesitant about a new option, ask directly about the condition that worries you most. You may find out whether it's just unfamiliar or presents a real difficulty.
overall.wands.02.reversed.pause: Don't put off your answer about something new until every worry is gone. The chance to take part could pass while you're still comparing options.

overall.wands.02.upright.headline: You could find a better opportunity beyond familiar places.
flow: There may be a chance to take something you're already doing further. Looking somewhere different could reveal a better offer or help you decide what to try next. Even if you don't make a change straight away, comparing your options will make the choice easier.
If somewhere interests you, find out whether you can actually go there or use what it offers. Check the new option before giving up what you're doing now.
overall.wands.02.upright.do: If you'd like to do what you're already doing somewhere else, find out whether it's possible and what would be better than where you are now.
overall.wands.02.upright.pause: Don't give up what you're doing just because a new option looks appealing. Keep it going until you've checked that you can actually start the new one.

overall.wands.03.reversed.headline: A delayed result could hold up what comes next.
flow: News you're expecting may arrive late, slowing things down today. A promising proposal could stall, or something may not grow as much as you'd hoped. Trying to meet the date you originally had in mind could put you under too much pressure.
While you wait, take care of what you can do now. Don't take on anything else when you still haven't had a definite answer.
overall.wands.03.reversed.do: If an answer you're waiting for is late, start with tasks you can handle without that answer.
overall.wands.03.reversed.pause: Don't take on something new on the assumption that what you're waiting for will soon work out. If it takes longer, you could have to finish both at once and struggle with the extra work.

overall.wands.03.upright.headline: Your preparations could bring results and open up more opportunities.
flow: Something you've already started could make further progress today. A response you've been waiting for may arrive, or an invitation to work together could come from a place you haven't considered before. With another person's help, you may be able to do more with something you've managed alone.
If someone responds well, suggest what you could do together next. Once what you've started is becoming established, an offer from outside your usual circle is worth considering too.
overall.wands.03.upright.do: If something you've been doing gets a good response, suggest what you could do together next. Build the conversation around the part that interested the other person.
overall.wands.03.upright.pause: Don't immediately reject an offer to work together just because it comes from somewhere unfamiliar. Hear how you could help each other before deciding.

overall.wands.04.reversed.headline: Something simple could bring you pleasure and satisfaction.
flow: It could be a pleasant day even without a major event. You may celebrate a small achievement or share a laugh with people you feel comfortable around. Things may look a little different from what you expected and still give you plenty to enjoy.
Share something that's gone well with someone close to you. You don't need to cancel a happy occasion just because the preparations aren't perfect.
overall.wands.04.reversed.do: If something has gone well, however small it is, tell someone close to you and enjoy it together.
overall.wands.04.reversed.pause: Don't cancel enjoyable plans because the preparations fell short of your hopes. A simple gathering can still mean laughter with people you feel comfortable around.

overall.wands.04.upright.headline: You could finish something successfully and have time to enjoy yourself.
flow: Something you've worked hard on may come to a satisfactory end today. You could have a reason to celebrate with the people involved or enjoy yourself somewhere familiar. Finishing something that's been on your mind may let you relax for a while.
Share the good news with the people who have been waiting for it to be finished. There's no need to start over just to make something you've completed more impressive.
overall.wands.04.upright.do: Tell the people who worked alongside you that things have ended well. You can look back on the effort it took and enjoy the result together.
overall.wands.04.upright.pause: Don't rework something you've finished well just to make it look more impressive. If everything necessary is done, leave yourself time to rest too.

overall.wands.05.reversed.headline: You could get caught in an argument where the story keeps changing.
flow: The more you argue about something, the more tangled it may become today. Different accounts of the same event or attempts to pass the blame could get you into trouble you didn't expect. If you focus on winning the argument, you may miss the facts you need.
Start with information that can establish who did what. Don't join someone else's dispute after hearing only one side.
overall.wands.05.reversed.do: If accounts of the same event differ, start with facts you can check about who did what.
overall.wands.05.reversed.pause: Don't step into someone else's dispute after hearing only one side. Arguing on their behalf without knowing the circumstances could get you into trouble too.

overall.wands.05.upright.headline: Clashing opinions could make things noisy and unsettled.
flow: Competition or a difference of opinion may make it hard to reach a decision today. Even over something minor, several people may want to take charge or insist on different methods. There may be plenty of talk, but trying the suggestions will let you compare them.
Once you've shared your view, listen to the other person's reasons too. Trying one suggestion at a time before choosing could reduce arguments better than everyone talking at once.
overall.wands.05.upright.do: If you disagree about the best method, compare what each person has suggested. If talking isn't enough to judge, try the methods before choosing.
overall.wands.05.upright.pause: Don't interrupt the other person just because you favour different methods. Hearing why they chose theirs can help you avoid an argument that keeps going over the same ground.

overall.wands.06.reversed.headline: Recognition for your efforts could take a little longer.
flow: The praise or result you're hoping for may not arrive straight away. Something you thought you'd done well could receive little response, or someone else's good news may make your own achievement seem small. A late answer doesn't have to mean failure.
Wait for the announcement if the result hasn't been confirmed yet. Exaggerating what you've achieved to get a better response could leave you struggling to explain it later.
overall.wands.06.reversed.do: If the result you're waiting for isn't out yet, wait for a definite announcement. A slow response doesn't mean the work you've done was a failure.
overall.wands.06.reversed.pause: Don't exaggerate what you've achieved to win praise. It could put you in a difficult position later if people discover that your claims don't match what you actually did.

overall.wands.06.upright.headline: Your efforts could earn recognition and bring good news.
flow: A good result may give people a reason to congratulate you today. Something you've waited a long time for could be decided in your favour, or people may notice the work you've quietly put in. You can also hope for a favourable answer where you're competing for something.
If you get a good result, give credit to the people who helped. Enjoy what went well without comparing it with someone else's result when you share the news.
overall.wands.06.upright.do: When people congratulate you on a good result, thank those who helped and explain what they contributed.
overall.wands.06.upright.pause: Don't put down someone else's achievement while sharing your own good result. You can enjoy what your effort has brought without deciding who did better.

overall.wands.07.reversed.headline: Several demands at once could make you give up an important condition.
flow: Pressure from several people may lead you to take on something you don't want today. You could find yourself agreeing to a request you meant to refuse or accepting without an important condition. Trying to escape an uncomfortable moment may leave you with more to do later.
If you can't answer straight away, ask for time to think. Make clear what you can take on now, instead of trying to hear several requests at once.
overall.wands.07.reversed.do: If several people are asking for favours, ask for time to think instead of replying straight away. Decide what you can take on, then tell them how much you can do.
overall.wands.07.reversed.pause: Don't accept conditions you don't want just because refusing feels awkward. You may feel better in the moment but end up with more to do later.

overall.wands.07.upright.headline: You could stand your ground despite difficult demands.
flow: Obstacles may not be enough to push you aside today. What you've already done can support your case, and stating your wishes clearly could help you resist an unfair demand. Holding your position may take effort at first, but you're well placed to reach an acceptable outcome.
Calmly explain which points you can't give up. Describing the conditions you need to keep will help more than answering every remark with a challenge.
overall.wands.07.upright.do: If a demand is difficult to accept, calmly explain which points you can't compromise on and why.
overall.wands.07.upright.pause: Don't argue back at every irritating remark while responding to a demand. Picking over minor wording can make it harder to discuss the conditions you can't accept.

overall.wands.08.reversed.headline: Conflicting messages could delay something that was going well.
flow: People who spend time or work closely together may clash over what's been said today. The same instructions could be passed on differently, or a message sent in haste because of someone else's reaction could start an argument. Something you expected to move quickly may need another explanation.
If a message upsets you, ask what the person meant first. Passing someone else's words on to several people could spread a misunderstanding even faster.
overall.wands.08.reversed.do: If something someone says bothers you, ask them directly what they meant. Asking first can help you avoid an argument over a misunderstanding.
overall.wands.08.reversed.pause: Don't repeat something you've heard to several people without checking it. If its meaning changes in the telling, misunderstandings could arise among the people involved.

overall.wands.08.upright.headline: News you've been waiting for could arrive and bring quick progress.
flow: Several things that have been held up could get moving at once today. Delayed replies may come through quickly, with the next plans settled soon after. Anything that needs you to go somewhere or act in person could also be easier than you expect.
Check what's being asked and send the necessary reply on time. A series of messages doesn't mean you need to agree to them all before you've read them.
overall.wands.08.upright.do: When the news you've been waiting for arrives, check the details and give any needed reply on time. If the conversation moves on to arranging a time, say when you're available too.
overall.wands.08.upright.pause: Don't agree to details you haven't checked just because updates are coming one after another. Even when things move quickly, check each thing you're agreeing to.

overall.wands.09.reversed.headline: The same problem could hold you up again.
flow: Your usual approach may not work today, leaving you frustrated. An old difficulty could return, or you may be so cautious that you miss help you need. Simply holding on could leave a fixable problem unresolved for longer.
If the same method has failed twice, hear out a different approach. Don't turn away someone offering fresh help just because things went badly before.
overall.wands.09.reversed.do: If the same method keeps getting you stuck, explain what hasn't worked to someone with experience and ask about another approach.
overall.wands.09.reversed.pause: Don't push away someone offering help because a previous experience of receiving help went badly. First hear what they could do for you this time.

overall.wands.09.upright.headline: You could protect what you've worked on through another difficulty.
flow: Perseverance could pay off even if something takes a while to finish today. A familiar problem may return, but you could get past it more easily this time. Even if a final check remains, the work you've done so far hasn't been wasted.
For a familiar problem, look at how you solved it before. Skipping a check because you're nearly done could make you repeat the same mistake.
overall.wands.09.upright.do: If a familiar problem returns, think back to how you solved it. Trying the method that worked before could make the same problem easier to resolve.
overall.wands.09.upright.pause: Don't skip the final check because something is almost finished. Looking over what remains can reduce the chance of having to work on it again.

overall.wands.10.reversed.headline: Without sharing the work, you could miss something you need to finish.
flow: Several responsibilities may make it hard to finish things today. You could end up doing someone else's share, or a task nobody was assigned may fall to you at the last minute. Unless you say it's too much, others may assume you can keep taking on more.
Ask now for help with the parts you can't finish alone. Waiting until you're already late to say you can't do it will give the people involved less time to help.
overall.wands.10.reversed.do: If you can't finish something alone, say now which part you'd like someone else to take on. Asking early lets them set aside time to help.
overall.wands.10.reversed.pause: If your current tasks are too much, don't silently pick up work that hasn't been assigned to anyone. Others may assume you're comfortable taking on more.

overall.wands.10.upright.headline: You may get results while having a busy day with plenty to do.
flow: More things to do could leave you short of time today. Doing well may bring requests to take on more, or several finishing touches could pile up on something almost done. Getting results may leave you with less time to yourself.
If you already have plenty to do, tell anyone making a new request when you'd be available. Accepting everything because you can do it well could delay something important too.
overall.wands.10.upright.do: If a new request comes in when you already have plenty to do, work out how long the remaining tasks will take and say when you could start helping.
overall.wands.10.upright.pause: Don't agree to everything just because you can do each task well. Even familiar tasks can overlap and delay an important commitment you made first.

overall.wands.11.reversed.headline: Unconfirmed news could raise your hopes and lead to a wasted trip.
flow: Something you set out to do with excitement may fall short of expectations today. What you heard could be inaccurate, or a chance to take part may not have been confirmed yet. Changing your mind partway through could also surprise someone who agreed to join you.
When you first hear about an opportunity, check for an official announcement. Don't recommend it to other people as good news before it's confirmed.
overall.wands.11.reversed.do: If you've heard that you can join a new activity, check the official information to confirm that you actually can.
overall.wands.11.reversed.pause: Don't recommend an opportunity to others while the details are still unconfirmed. If you agree to join together and the details change, they could be caught off guard too.

overall.wands.11.upright.headline: Something you hear about could become an unexpected opportunity.
flow: A new piece of information may give you something worth trying today. You could hear useful news at a gathering you casually joined or get a chance to try an activity you've been curious about. Something small at first could become an enjoyable interest.
If something catches your interest, ask where and how you can try it. You don't have to put off starting because you think you should be good at it from the beginning.
overall.wands.11.upright.do: If you hear about an interesting activity, ask where and how you can take part so you can try it for yourself.
overall.wands.11.upright.pause: Don't keep putting off an activity because you feel you need to be good at it from the start. You can enjoy trying it for the first time without being skilled at it.

overall.wands.12.reversed.headline: A sudden change of mind could interrupt your plans.
flow: Something you start may be difficult to see through today. Someone who agreed to join you could drop out, or a hastily arranged visit may be cancelled, leaving you with a wasted trip. Arranging something else on the spot to make up for it could go wrong again.
Before setting off, check that things are still going ahead. If you can no longer go yourself, let the other person know straight away.
overall.wands.12.reversed.do: If you've arranged to meet someone or visit them, check with them before setting off that it's still going ahead.
overall.wands.12.reversed.pause: Don't rush to make another arrangement just because one was cancelled. Checking that the other person is available before deciding can reduce the chance of changing the new plan too.

overall.wands.12.upright.headline: Taking action yourself could bring quick progress.
flow: Getting out and doing something could be rewarding today. A visit you've put off or a new activity may go better than expected, and you could settle in quickly somewhere unfamiliar and enjoy the experience. Trying something you've spent a long time considering may make the answer clearer.
If there's somewhere you've wanted to visit, check when you can go and make the trip. Planning too many stops in your excitement could leave you little time to enjoy them.
overall.wands.12.upright.do: If there's somewhere you've wanted to visit, find out when you can go and make the trip.
overall.wands.12.upright.pause: Don't plan too many stops in one day just because you're excited. Rushing to the next place could leave you less time to stay and enjoy where you are.

overall.wands.13.reversed.headline: Worrying about people's reactions could make things uncomfortable.
flow: People may be less receptive to what you want than usual today. Someone else getting more attention could hurt your feelings, or a quiet response may make your tone sharper. Trying too hard to gain recognition could leave people even less interested.
After speaking, give the other person time to share their thoughts too. Pointing out faults when someone is being praised could leave others with a worse impression of you.
overall.wands.13.reversed.do: After you've shared your thoughts, give the other person a chance to speak and hear them out instead of adding more of your own.
overall.wands.13.reversed.pause: Don't add a criticism when someone else is being praised. People listening may see it as an attempt to put that person down.

overall.wands.13.upright.headline: People could respond warmly and make the day enjoyable.
flow: You may find a welcoming face wherever you go today. Something you bring up could draw interest, and an invitation to do something together is likely to receive a good response. You may have a chance to show what you do well without having to force it.
If there's something you'd like to say to a group, feel free to bring it up. Give others time to join in too, so everyone can enjoy the conversation.
overall.wands.13.upright.do: If there's something you'd like to share while spending time with a group, feel free to bring it up first.
overall.wands.13.upright.pause: Don't keep talking only about yourself because people are responding well. Pausing to let others join in can make the conversation more enjoyable.

overall.wands.14.reversed.headline: Standards that are too high could hold things up.
flow: You may find it hard to finish because even a good result doesn't satisfy you today. Asking too much of the people involved or focusing on a minor shortcoming could delay a decision. Even a well-meant comment may sound like too much interference.
Separate what must be corrected from what can stay as it is. Insisting on your own way could make it hard for people who've been helpful to keep contributing.
overall.wands.14.reversed.do: If a result doesn't satisfy you, look at the parts you want changed. If those changes aren't necessary, it's fine to call it finished.
overall.wands.14.reversed.pause: Don't make someone redo parts they've done well just because they're slightly different from your way. Excessive demands could make it hard for even a willing helper to continue.

overall.wands.14.upright.headline: Taking the lead could bring support and good results.
flow: Something you lead could go well today. Explain clearly what you want to do and people may join you, helping something you've hesitated over get past its first difficulty. Doing what you said you would can earn people's trust.
Start by keeping the commitments you said you could manage. Giving the people who joined you the parts they do well could make it easier to finish.
overall.wands.14.upright.do: If you're in charge of something you're starting together, first ask what each person does well, then divide the work accordingly.
overall.wands.14.upright.pause: Don't get things started and expect others to sort out everything that follows. Even when you've divided the work by ability, follow through on the part you promised to do.

text: A lack of ideas for an assignment could delay your start. Trying to force an impressive answer may make even the basic content hard to organise. Start with a short answer to what's being asked.
At work, new ideas may be hard to find, or a suggestion could receive less enthusiasm than you hoped. Fill in what's needed first instead of trying to complete an ambitious plan in one go.

Ideas for writing or creative work may come readily, making an assignment easier. It's also a good day to understand and enjoy something you're learning for the first time. Writing down your ideas can help you see which topic to develop.
At work, a fresh suggestion could receive a good response. Even in a task you're handling for the first time, comfortable conversations with others may bring help.
Disagreements over an assignment with a friend could delay completion. If only one person does the explaining or summarising, studying together may be less useful too.

At work, different goals could mean having to do the same task again. Even if you thought cooperation was going well, the other person may have understood things differently. Check directly what each of you is handling and what result you want.

Explaining problems to each other as you study with a friend could help you understand faster than studying alone. Your different strengths may also complement each other in a group presentation and earn a good assessment.

At work, you and the person you're working with may want the same things, making the task easier. It's a good day to talk things through with a colleague you've disagreed with too. Discussing what you'll achieve together can make agreement easier.

An attempt to study together could turn into a long chat with little progress. If exam preparation or a group assignment still needs doing, don't put it off simply because you're meeting close friends.

At work, gossip from a gathering or people taking sides could make cooperation uncomfortable. Sharing information only with friends may leave someone else without what they need. Keep everyone involved informed about the work.
A presentation or assignment prepared together could receive a good assessment. It's a good day to celebrate exam results with study friends or share encouraging news.
At work, a team effort could bring results and congratulations. If colleagues helped you finish a task, share the pleasure with them. The good mood may make your next collaboration easier too.
A new explanation could make something you didn't understand before fall into place. It's a good day to return to a subject or assignment you set aside.

At work, a postponed task may resume, or you could reconsider a proposal you passed over. Benefits you didn't notice before may help you see an opportunity. Check the changed conditions before deciding whether to take part.

Boredom with studying may make it hard to remember what you've read. Tuning out a lesson because the topic seems familiar could also mean missing an explanation you need for an exam. Try a few problems yourself to check your understanding.
At work, handling a routine task without much thought could cause a small mistake. Dismissing a new proposal without interest may also mean missing an opportunity that suits you.
A disappointing exam could help you identify what needs improving. Taking on board a teacher's or friend's explanation may make the same type of question easier than before.

At work, a way to revive something that went badly could emerge. Apologies may also clear up a conversation that went wrong with a colleague. Ask for the help you need instead of sitting alone blaming yourself.

An exam or assignment result may fall short of your hopes. Getting a few questions wrong doesn't mean you're weak at the whole subject. Checking why the answers were wrong can show you what to work on next.
At work, a proposal you had hopes for may be declined, or part of a project could fall through. The entire achievement may not be lost, so check which parts can continue.

A method that worked well before may not fit the question you're facing now. If the question's conditions or the material have changed, don't reach straight for the familiar answer. Checking the new explanation can reveal a difference you missed.
At work, copying a method that succeeded in the past could bring requests for changes. A method that once worked may not suit today's customers or colleagues, so hear what they need now.

Remembering something you learned before could make a problem easy to solve. Even a question you got wrong long ago may make more sense when you revisit it. Material you've revised could lead to good marks in an exam.
At work, a former colleague or familiar experience could prove helpful. Looking at a past example may reveal an approach you can use on a task that's currently stuck.
You could resolve confusion between different explanations and reach a clear understanding. Choosing a solution method that suits you may also help you answer questions faster.

At work, a decision could be made about which of several proposals to pursue. Setting aside unlikely proposals may make the results of your own work clearer. It's a good day to finish the task you've decided on.

Despite plenty of studying, you may find few questions you can solve on your own. Following only predicted exam questions could leave you stuck when a different type appears. Choose one study resource and work to understand it fully.
At work, many proposals may sound promising, but few may be ready to carry out. Check the time and conditions needed before imagining the good results.
More hours of study may not raise your marks as much as you hoped. If you're repeating the same material because you don't want to change a familiar explanation, hear a different approach too.

At work, a task you'd agreed to stop handling could return and become a burden. Waiting on a promise that things will change may leave you with the same complaints. Check whether the responsibilities can actually be shared.

The studying you've done so far may not bring the results you want. It's time to seek another explanation instead of holding on to material or classes that don't suit you. Choosing what you actually need could help you understand a difficult part.
At work, your current role may end, or you could be offered different work. If a task has continued without results, make a clear decision about whether to carry on or bring it to a close.

High expectations may make you dissatisfied even with decent marks. Comparing scores with others could keep you from noticing where you've improved. Look separately at subjects that need work and those you've done well in.
At work, finishing a task or receiving praise may still disappoint you if the reward differs from what you expected. Don't expect one good assessment to change every condition to your liking.
You can hope for the result you wanted in an exam or assignment you've prepared for. Even difficult questions may go well, bringing satisfaction that reflects your studying.

At work, sustained effort could bring results and the assessment you wanted. If a proposal succeeds or your performance brings good results, let yourself enjoy it. Thanking those who helped is a good way to share the pleasure.
Different views could delay an assignment even among close friends. Assuming everyone will know what to do may leave gaps. Say clearly what you need to ask of them, even if it feels uncomfortable.
At work, complaints within the team could surface despite apparent cooperation. Covering up a problem to keep the mood pleasant may lead to another clash over the same task.
Support from those around you could let you study comfortably and show what you can do. Working well together on a presentation or assignment may also bring a good result.

At work, cooperation with colleagues could produce steady results. It's a good day to receive recognition for a shared achievement and exchange happy news. Relationships in which you've regularly helped each other may feel reassuring.

Ideas may come to you but prove hard to organise into an essay or answer. Writing down whatever comes to mind could take you away from the assignment's requirements. First check which question you're answering.
At work, an offhand remark could be misunderstood, or a proposal may be judged underdeveloped. Ask what's missing before showing your hurt at the criticism.
A new idea could make a writing or presentation assignment enjoyable. Even a seemingly odd question may offer a clue that helps you understand a concept.

At work, a small idea could attract interest, or you may be offered something you've never tried. An idea doesn't need to be perfectly developed to meet a need. A simple example will help get its meaning across.

Even a beautifully written answer may earn disappointing marks if the reasoning is weak. Confidently explaining something you don't know well in a presentation could leave you stuck on follow-up questions. Start with what you actually understand.
At work, a proposal that sounded appealing may not happen, or promised support could be delayed. Don't finalise your entire schedule on the strength of the other person's words alone.
An assignment expressing ideas through speech or writing could receive a good response. In a presentation, including what listeners are likely to wonder about will help your explanation reach them.

At work, you may be offered work you're pleased to take on or invited to work together. An idea you explain sincerely could also be considered favourably. Discuss exactly what each of you expects to do.

Concern about other people's moods or requests may make it hard to retain what you study. Helping with someone else's assignment at the expense of your own preparation could bring a disappointing exam result.

At work, looking after a colleague's tasks too much could delay your own. Saying you're fine when you're struggling may leave you suddenly hurt by a small remark. Be honest about how much help you can give now.
An explanation that addresses exactly where you're struggling could help your studies progress. Feeling comfortable asking questions may let you understand something you couldn't work out alone.

At work, you could receive a good assessment for noticing what someone wants. Conversations may go smoothly in roles involving customer contact or listening to others' views. Attending to even small difficulties can build trust.

Assuming only your favourite subjects will go well could make your preparation uneven. Skipping an explanation of a wrong answer because you don't want to hear it may leave the same mistake uncorrected. Base your studying on which answers you actually get right, rather than how you feel.
At work, emotional remarks that dodge responsibility could complicate a discussion. Getting angry at a colleague who points out a needed correction may make the problem harder to solve.
You could calmly show what you've practised in an exam or presentation, even if you feel nervous. Starting with what you know may help you develop an answer to a difficult question.

At work, calmly sorting through conflicting views could earn trust. Hearing the other person's circumstances while making necessary decisions without delay may make the work easier. A role with responsibility could bring a good assessment too.

Rushing in a test could cost you points on questions you know how to answer. Skipping part of a question or copying an answer incorrectly may lead to mistakes. Review what you've answered instead of trying to finish as quickly as possible.

At work, pushing ahead too fast could bring requests for changes or friction with colleagues. Rushing others to meet a schedule you set alone may make cooperation harder. Finish your current work before taking on more.

Tests could give you a good chance to show what you've learned. You may solve a problem that's been difficult or receive a good assessment for a presentation you've prepared. An assignment you've put off because it seemed hard is worth another attempt today.

At work, delayed tasks could move forward and you may finish what you've been assigned. A proposal of yours could be well received when several are being considered. If you're clear on what needs doing, it's a good day to put your ideas forward with confidence.

Studying in the same way may do little to reduce recurring mistakes. Rereading a familiar explanation you don't understand could bring little progress for the time spent. You need to consider a different way of solving the problem.

At work, holding on to a task that should already be finished could delay the next one. Keeping the old method after its problems become clear may bring the same requests for corrections. First check how the requirements have changed.

A familiar way of solving problems may stop working, prompting a change in how you study. Leaving an unproductive exercise behind and hearing a new explanation could change your understanding. If an assignment needs finishing, it's a good day to complete it and move on to the next part of your studies.

At work, a task may come to an end or your responsibilities could change. If a plan you expected to continue is closed down, you'll still need to finish the remaining details, however disappointing that feels. Find out what your next role involves instead of holding on to work that's ended.

Distractions could ease, allowing you to catch up on studying. A problem you've kept putting off may be easier than expected once you tackle it today. It's a good time to break one habit that interrupts your study.

At work, you may be able to share an unmanageable task or step away from unnecessary competition. With less extra work to carry, you could start getting results in your own role again. Explain clearly when you can't meet a request.

Pressure to improve your marks could make even material you've studied seem confusing. Focusing on whether you've done more than others may keep you from understanding why an answer was wrong. Don't cut back on sleep to force yourself through more material.

At work, the burden could become excessive even if you're getting results. Promising more than you can handle in pursuit of success may leave you with difficulties after the initial praise. Don't give up necessary rest for a good assessment.

Insisting on a familiar method could leave you stuck on a new question type. If a teacher or friend offers a different explanation, hear it before deciding it's wrong. Repeating a method that doesn't fit the question is unlikely to produce the answer.

At work, one-sided instructions or excessive interference could cause delays. Competing over who's right may stop the actual work today. Even if you're in charge, listen when colleagues explain their circumstances.

If you've mastered the basics, you're well placed for a solid exam result. Applying the principles you've learned in order may let you solve even a difficult problem without becoming unsettled. Calmly follow a familiar solution through to the end.

At work, careful completion of your responsibilities could earn trust. Tasks with clear timing and roles may proceed smoothly. If you've taken on a major responsibility, you could make the necessary decisions calmly too.

Even a well-presented assignment may receive a disappointing assessment if its content is thin. Focusing on length could keep you from answering the actual question. Fill in the main explanation before improving the appearance.

At work, looking after others could make you miss your own deadline. However much you've helped, late work may lead to an assessment below your hopes. Check what's left on your own list before accepting a request.

Assignments expressing ideas through writing or drawing could bring good results. Several ideas may come to you even on a topic you've struggled with, helping you develop the content. Carefully prepared creative work or a presentation could receive praise.

At work, a plan prepared over a long time could produce concrete results. A proposal that considers people's tastes or needs may receive a good response today. If the achievement is shared, recognise your colleagues' contributions too.

Careless reading of an exam question or a missed assignment requirement could cost marks. Even on a familiar topic, read to the end to see what answer is required. Luck is unlikely to make up for unprepared areas today.

At work, starting without checking could bring an unexpected problem. Assuming a new task is easy may leave you asking for help just before the deadline. Find out the time and conditions needed before beginning.

Something you're learning for the first time may be easier to understand than expected. An unfamiliar subject or new class could help you discover a field that suits you today. Asking straight away about anything unclear will make the next stage of study easier too.

At work, you could encounter an unfamiliar task or a new suggestion. Even without experience, starting may reveal something that suits you unexpectedly well. Don't casually agree to conditions you haven't checked yet.

Long hours with a book may feel frustrating if your understanding isn't improving. Simply rereading the same explanation can leave you stuck on the same questions. Pinpoint where you're getting lost and seek a different explanation.

At work, unnecessary waiting or repeated concessions by just one side could leave a task at a standstill. If you're only told to keep waiting, it's time to ask what still needs doing. Taking on everyone else's share won't solve every problem.

Your studying may not show immediate results, but a different solution could help you understand. Setting aside a stubborn problem briefly and revisiting an example may reveal something you missed. Slow progress today doesn't mean you've stopped learning.

At work, an important decision may be delayed. Hearing more about the other person's circumstances could explain why discussions have stalled. Allowing the time needed may help you reach a better agreement than pressing for an answer today.

Studying alone could leave a misunderstanding uncorrected for a long time. Without asking about what you don't know, you may keep making the same mistake. Someone else's explanation could reveal why you're stuck.

At work, keeping progress to yourself could delay cooperation. Hiding a problem because you don't want help may also reduce the time available to solve it. It's better to say where you're stuck, even briefly.

Focused study on your own could bring results today. Following a difficult concept carefully may let you understand it well enough to explain to someone else. Time to work through it on your own will help more than racing through material with others.

At work, concentrating on a problem could reveal an important answer. Research or analysis requiring depth may give you a good chance to use your skills. Checking thoroughly before offering a view will make the explanation reliable.

An explanation different from the usual one could make a difficult concept clear. Even if a new method suits you, keep to the answer format required by the exam. A method isn't correct simply because it's new.

At work, a suggestion that differs from the existing approach could divide opinions. Even a necessary change may not be accepted immediately if it breaks with usual practice. A real example of what improves can help persuade people.

A teacher's explanation or the basics in a textbook could solve a problem you're stuck on. Following the sequence you've learned may make solitary study less confusing. Good exam results are also worth hoping for if you've kept hold of the basic concepts.

At work, following established procedures could keep a task progressing steadily. An experienced colleague's advice may help with unfamiliar work. Meeting agreed standards can make a review or approval easier to obtain.

You may read a sentence but miss its main meaning and answer incorrectly. Choosing an answer just because you recognise a word could make you mistake one concept for another. Don't pretend to understand a part you haven't grasped.

At work, skimming material could make you miss something important. Guessing unspoken circumstances may also lead you to misunderstand a colleague's intention. It's better not to delay a question that needs checking.

Quiet study could help you understand a complicated concept deeply today. Careful reading may also reveal a hidden condition in a question. Fully understanding one problem is likely to bring more progress than rushing through many.

At work, a close look at material could reveal something others missed. Information that hasn't been released yet may delay an important decision. Separating what you know from what you guess will make your report more trustworthy.

Without checking why an answer was wrong, you could repeat the same mistake even on a familiar question. Blaming only the questions or the marking for disappointing results may hide what you need to improve. Start by reviewing your own solution.

At work, refusing to acknowledge a past mistake could delay an assessment or discussion. Even if you dislike someone's judgement, don't reject necessary corrections too. Putting the mistake right can allow the discussion to continue.

Trying a question you got wrong before could bring a better result. If you have a resit or a chance to revise an assignment, it's a good day to show what you can do again. Understanding the cause of a past mistake can help you avoid losing marks the same way.

At work, a delayed assessment may arrive or a resubmitted proposal could be considered. If you've fixed a previous problem, the improvement in your results may be recognised. Explain clearly what you've improved.
